name: Photovoltaic Cascade Rifle PCR-3 'Tithe'
description:
The PCR-3 operates on an unusual energy principle: rather than generating its own destructive output, it catalyzes a photovoltaic cascade reaction in surfaces it strikes. A precisely modulated ultraviolet primer beam is fired first, lasting approximately 12 milliseconds, which seeds the target surface with a resonant photoelectric charge. A second, high-intensity visible-spectrum pulse follows immediately, triggering an explosive release of that stored charge across the target's surface area. The result is a directed electrical detonation that originates from the target itself rather than the weapon — armor and shielding that would normally absorb or deflect an incoming energy beam instead become the source of the discharge.

Helix Biosystems developed the PCR-3 as part of a research program into photovoltaic energy harvesting, and the weapon represents a militarized accident — a researcher demonstrated that the cascade reaction could be induced in organic tissue, which has its own weak photovoltaic properties due to melanin and porphyrin compounds in skin and muscle. On living targets, the electrical detonation produces severe burns and cardiac disruption from the inside out. On synthetic materials — particularly the photoreactive polymers used in common body armor — the effect is even more dramatic, causing catastrophic structural failure of the armor itself.

The Tithe's form is elegant and slender, a long-barreled rifle with a dual-emitter muzzle that houses both the UV primer and the visible-spectrum trigger. The barrel is unusually cool to the touch even after sustained use, as the weapon itself generates relatively little waste heat — the energy is deposited in the target. This gives the PCR-3 a deceptively benign appearance that has made it a favorite of collectors and a headache for customs enforcement.
specifications: effective range: Up to 340m primer beam duration: 12ms UV pulse trigger pulse: High-intensity visible spectrum, 580–620nm cascade reaction delay: ~3ms between primer and trigger power cell: Helix HL-12 dual-channel cell, 18 complete shot pairs weight: 5.2kg dimensions: 112cm length anti-armor performance: Exceptional against photoreactive polymer armor; moderate against ceramic plate thermal signature: Very low
tactical_use: The PCR-3 excels at long-range anti-personnel and anti-armor engagements where the target's own materials are weaponized against them. Operators are trained to identify armor composition before engaging — the weapon is most effective against modern photoreactive composite armors and least effective against old-fashioned ceramic or metal plate. The low thermal signature and absence of a visible beam (the UV primer is invisible, the trigger pulse brief) makes the Tithe an excellent ambush weapon at range. Licensed military snipers use it for anti-material work when they need to deny an enemy position's equipment.
cultural_context: The PCR-3's licensing requirement and high price point make it a weapon of elite military and paramilitary units. In GLMZ, possessing a licensed Tithe is a mark of institutional legitimacy — it signals that the carrier has the corporate or governmental backing to navigate the licensing bureaucracy. Unlicensed copies occasionally surface on the black market, but the dual-emitter calibration is difficult to replicate, and bootleg versions frequently misfire, seeding the operator with the cascade charge instead of the target. Stories of bootleg Tithe accidents — operators detonating their own armor — are common enough to have become cautionary urban legend.
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions licensed sniper teams
Helix Biosystems internal security (prototype testing units)
Elite mercenary companies with government contracts
Collectors and high-tier black market brokers
story_hooks: A licensed PCR-3 is recovered from a civilian massacre. The license traces to a corporate security division that officially disbanded two years ago — but the license was renewed last month by someone with deep system access.

A street-level arms dealer is selling what they claim are PCR-3s at a fraction of market price. Three buyers have already been hospitalized with inside-out burn injuries. The dealer doesn't know the units are miscalibrated — or does they?

Helix Biosystems is quietly recalling a specific production batch of PCR-3s, citing 'calibration variance.' The real reason: a flaw in that batch makes the primer beam interact with a specific neural implant brand, seeding the implant with a cascade charge that can be remotely triggered.
related_entities: Tessera Industries Phantom Comms Relay PCR-3

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, elongated precision rifle with an almost medical aesthetic — more laboratory instrument than traditional firearm. The profile is intentionally slim and balanced, suggesting advanced engineering rather than raw power. The dual-emitter muzzle is distinctly unusual, housing two precision optical elements in tight parallel alignment.
physical_description.dimensions: 112cm overall length, 48cm barrel, 8cm width at receiver, 6cm height at scope rail
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 5.2kg — feels balanced and almost delicate in trained hands, lacking the heft expected of a weapon system. Excellent weight distribution creates a sensation of effortless control.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite chassis with anodized aluminum receiver and optical housings. Barrel features a polished fused-silica lens array.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite with brushed silver aluminum accents. The dual emitters feature brilliant optical black coating to minimize reflectivity. Minimal weathering on well-maintained examples.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray composite primary with silver-gray metallic accents. Emitter housings in deep matte black. Helix branding in phosphorescent cyan.
physical_description.grip_texture: Stippled polymer grip with ergonomic finger grooves, cool to the touch. Magazine well reinforced with textured aluminum. Charging handle wrapped in thin synthetic cord.
distinctive_features: Dual-emitter muzzle with separated UV primer and visible-spectrum trigger optics
Unusual lack of heat venting or thermal dissipation design — weapon generates minimal waste heat
Transparent capacitor housing on left side showing glowing HL-12 power cell with dual-channel indicator lights
Precision graduated reticle with photovoltaic-reactive target compensation markers
Minimal mechanical controls — most functions are electronic and gesture-responsive
Faint phosphorescent charging status along the receiver spine
Custom engraved nomenclature: 'PCR-3 TITHE' with Helix biometric lock indent
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Helix Biosystems logo embossed on left receiver. Serial number etched in UV-reactive ink on capacitor housing. Regulatory licensing stamp — cyan Φ currency symbol with 'LICENSED' — on right side of mag well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate. The Tithe is a precision instrument maintained obsessively by its operators. Even field-used examples show minimal wear; users favor careful cleaning and inspection over rugged durability. Collectors keep them in near-pristine condition.
